dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the admissibility predicate whose satisfying scales t form the set on the right-hand side and, after unfolding LocalDef002, also the set implicit on the left-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For mu and X, this is defined to be the infimum in ENNReal of the set of scales t satisfying LocalDef001 mu X t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The left side is definitionally the same infimum displayed on the right, so the proposition is an unfolding identity rather than a substantive estimate.

binders: An arbitrary measurable-space structure on Omega.
An arbitrary measure mu on that measurable space.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Omega → Real.
conclusions: LocalDef002(mu, X) equals the infimum, in the extended nonnegative reals, of all t such that X is measurable, t is neither zero nor infinity, omega ↦ exp(|X(omega)| / t.toReal) is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2.
mathematical_definitions: For t in [0, infinity], define A(mu, X, t) to mean: X is Borel-measurable; t ≠ 0; t ≠ infinity; the real-valued function omega ↦ exp(|X(omega)| / t.toReal) is mu-integrable; and ∫ exp(|X(omega)| / t.toReal) dmu(omega) ≤ 2.
LocalDef002(mu, X) is defined as inf {t in ENNReal | A(mu, X, t)}.
The infimum is taken in the complete linear order ENNReal, the nonnegative reals with an added infinity element.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Omega, every measure mu on it, and every real-valued function X, the quantity LocalDef002(mu, X) is exactly the extended-nonnegative-real infimum of the finite nonzero scales t for which X is measurable and the exponential moment integral ∫ exp(|X|/t) dmu is defined by an integrable real function and is at most 2. Since LocalDef002 is itself defined to be this exact infimum, the asserted equality is definitional.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure mu is arbitrary; the statement does not require mu to be a probability measure or even finite.
The function X is arbitrary at theorem level. Measurability is imposed inside the admissibility predicate, so if X is not measurable then no t is admissible.
There is no hypothesis that any admissible t exists. The complete-order convention for the infimum of an empty set therefore matters and can make the value infinity.
Admissible t must be neither zero nor infinity; the denominator is the real conversion t.toReal.
Integrability of the exponential function is an explicit separate conjunct in addition to the numerical integral bound.
The theorem is true by unfolding LocalDef002 and establishes no estimate, positivity, finiteness, attainment of the infimum, or norm properties.
No assumption that X is a random variable on a probability space is encoded beyond the optional measurability conjunct inside the admissible-scale set.
